title: Bar Exam Scandal of The Century

author: LegalEagle
description:
Russell Brand’s own barrister asked him in front of the jury whether a single person would testify on his behalf. He said no.

Brand told the jury that friends and colleagues had abandoned him. The prosecution pushed back, pointing to his millions of followers and a show he played to around 2,000 people after the documentary aired.

Both the US and England let defendants force witnesses into court, through the Sixth Amendment right to compulsory process in the US and a witness summons in England. But dragging an unwilling witness onto the stand is usually a terrible idea, because you can’t predict what they’ll say, and their testimony is rarely helpful.

So why ask the question at all? Our guess, and it’s only a guess, is that the defense wanted to explain an empty witness list before the prosecution could.
